<!-- Generated by `idiotproof agent export` (or `idiotproof-mcp --export-tools`). Do not hand-edit. -->

## `account_activities`

Account activity log: fills, dividends, fees, deposits, interest, option expirations/assignments (newest first, ET).

CLI equivalent: idiotproof account activities [--since <date>] [--until <date>] [--type <string[]>] [--limit <int>] [--mode <all|paper|live>]
Examples:
  idiotproof account activities
  idiotproof account activities --since 2026-10-01 --type FILL --mode paper
  idiotproof account activities --type DIV,FEE,INT

Read-only. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Account activity log: fills, dividends, fees, deposits, interest, option expirations/assignments (newest first, ET).",
  "properties": {
    "since": {
      "type": "string",
      "format": "date",
      "description": "First ET date to include, yyyy-MM-dd (default: 7 days ago)."
    },
    "until": {
      "type": "string",
      "format": "date",
      "description": "Last ET date to include, yyyy-MM-dd (default: today)."
    },
    "type": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "description": "Activity types, comma-separated: FILL, DIV, FEE, CSD (deposit), CSW (withdrawal), JNLC, INT, OPEXP, OPASN, ... (default: all)."
    },
    "limit": {
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Most rows per account, newest first (default 100, max 1000).",
      "default": 100
    },
    "mode": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "all",
        "paper",
        "live"
      ],
      "description": "paper, live or all (default all).",
      "default": "all"
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

## `account_buying_power`

Buying power by kind (overall, Reg T, day-trading, non-marginable, options), cash and margin multiplier.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof account buying-power [--mode <all|paper|live>]
Examples:
  idiotproof account buying-power
  idiotproof account buying-power --mode live

Read-only. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Buying power by kind (overall, Reg T, day-trading, non-marginable, options), cash and margin multiplier.",
  "properties": {
    "mode": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "all",
        "paper",
        "live"
      ],
      "description": "paper, live or all (default all).",
      "default": "all"
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

## `account_calendar`

Trading days with premarket, regular and after-hours times (ET); early closes and holidays called out.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof account calendar [--from <date>] [--to <date>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>]
Examples:
  idiotproof account calendar
  idiotproof account calendar --from 2026-11-20 --to 2026-12-31

Read-only. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Trading days with premarket, regular and after-hours times (ET); early closes and holidays called out.",
  "properties": {
    "from": {
      "type": "string",
      "format": "date",
      "description": "First date, yyyy-MM-dd (default today ET)."
    },
    "to": {
      "type": "string",
      "format": "date",
      "description": "Last date, yyyy-MM-dd (default 14 days after --from)."
    },
    "mode": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "sandbox",
        "paper",
        "live"
      ],
      "description": "Which Alpaca account\u0027s keys ask: paper or live (default paper; the calendar is the same).",
      "default": "paper"
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

## `account_config_set`

Change one Alpaca account setting (Live needs a confirmation code).

CLI equivalent: idiotproof account config set <setting> <value> [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>]
Examples:
  idiotproof account config set no_shorting true
  idiotproof account config set max_margin_multiplier 1 --mode live

Changes saved state. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Change one Alpaca account setting (Live needs a confirmation code).",
  "properties": {
    "setting": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "dtbp_check, pdt_check, trade_confirm_email, suspend_trade, no_shorting, fractional_trading, max_margin_multiplier, max_options_trading_level or ptp_no_exception_entry.",
      "default": ""
    },
    "value": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The new value (see \u0060account config\u0060 for each setting\u0027s meaning).",
      "default": ""
    },
    "mode": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "sandbox",
        "paper",
        "live"
      ],
      "description": "paper or live (default paper; live needs a confirmation code).",
      "default": "paper"
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "setting",
    "value"
  ]
}
```

## `account_history`

Equity over time as a Braille line chart, with the true P&L (deposits excluded) for 1D to all-time windows.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof account history [--period <string>] [--timeframe <string>] [--extended] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--width <int>] [--height <int>]
Examples:
  idiotproof account history
  idiotproof account history --period 1D --timeframe 5Min --extended
  idiotproof account history --period 1A --mode live

Read-only. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Equity over time as a Braille line chart, with the true P\u0026L (deposits excluded) for 1D to all-time windows.",
  "properties": {
    "period": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Window: \u003Cn\u003ED, \u003Cn\u003EW, \u003Cn\u003EM or \u003Cn\u003EA (years), or all (default 1M).",
      "default": "1M"
    },
    "timeframe": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Point spacing: 1Min, 5Min, 15Min, 1H or 1D (default: Alpaca\u0027s choice for the period)."
    },
    "extended": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Include premarket and after-hours in intraday history (default regular hours only).",
      "default": false
    },
    "mode": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "sandbox",
        "paper",
        "live"
      ],
      "description": "paper or live (default paper).",
      "default": "paper"
    },
    "width": {
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Chart width in characters (default: the terminal\u0027s, else 118)."
    },
    "height": {
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Chart rows (default 16).",
      "default": 16
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

## `assets_bonds`

Alpaca fixed income assets: US Treasuries or US corporate bonds with coupon, maturity, last close and yield.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof assets bonds [--type <treasuries|corporates>] [--subtype <string>] [--bond-status <string>] [--cusips <string[]>] [--isins <string[]>] [--search <string>] [--limit <int>] [--mode <paper|live>]
Examples:
  idiotproof assets bonds --subtype bill --limit 20
  idiotproof assets bonds --type corporates --search AAPL

Read-only. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Alpaca fixed income assets: US Treasuries or US corporate bonds with coupon, maturity, last close and yield.",
  "properties": {
    "type": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "treasuries",
        "corporates"
      ],
```

## `crypto_buy`

Buy a crypto pair (fractional, GTC/IOC) through the TransactionGateway. Paper by default; live needs a confirmation code.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof crypto buy <pair> [<qty>] [--notional <decimal>] [--limit <decimal>] [--trigger <decimal>] [--stop <decimal>] [--target <decimal>] [--tif <string>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--note <string>]
Examples:
  idiotproof crypto buy BTC/USD 0.001 --limit 70000 --stop 66500
  idiotproof crypto buy ETH/USD --notional 250 --stop 2300 --mode live

MOVES MONEY. Sandbox and Paper run immediately. A Live action returns status confirmation-required with a preview and a code instead of executing: show the user the preview verbatim, ask them, and only if they say yes call this tool again with the identical arguments plus confirmation_code. Never invent or reuse a code. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Buy a crypto pair (fractional, GTC/IOC) through the TransactionGateway. Paper by default; live needs a confirmation code.",
  "properties": {
    "pair": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Crypto pair, e.g. BTC/USD.",
      "default": ""
    },
    "qty": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Coin quantity, fractional allowed (0.0015). Leave out and pass --notional to size by dollars."
    },
    "notional": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Size by dollar amount instead of coin quantity."
    },
    "limit": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Limit price. Without it the order is a market order."
    },
    "trigger": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Stop trigger price: with --limit it makes a stop-limit order."
    },
    "stop": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Protective stop price for a buy; the Risk Guardian refuses entries without one."
    },
    "target": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Take-profit price (for the reward:risk check)."
    },
    "tif": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Time in force: gtc (default) or ioc.",
      "default": "gtc"
    },
    "mode": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "sandbox",
        "paper",
        "live"
      ],
      "description": "paper (default) or live (needs a confirmation code). Sandbox does not simulate crypto.",
      "default": "paper"
    },
    "note": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Why: kept in the audit trail."
    },
    "confirmation_code": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Only after the user explicitly approves the preview: the code a previous call of this tool returned."
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "pair"
  ]
}
```

## `crypto_sell`

Sell crypto you hold (crypto is long-only). Exits always clear the gates; live needs a confirmation code.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof crypto sell <pair> [<qty>] [--notional <decimal>] [--limit <decimal>] [--trigger <decimal>] [--stop <decimal>] [--target <decimal>] [--tif <string>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--note <string>]
Examples:
  idiotproof crypto sell BTC/USD 0.001
  idiotproof crypto sell ETH/USD --notional 100 --limit 2600 --tif ioc --mode live

MOVES MONEY. Sandbox and Paper run immediately. A Live action returns status confirmation-required with a preview and a code instead of executing: show the user the preview verbatim, ask them, and only if they say yes call this tool again with the identical arguments plus confirmation_code. Never invent or reuse a code. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Sell crypto you hold (crypto is long-only). Exits always clear the gates; live needs a confirmation code.",
  "properties": {
    "pair": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Crypto pair, e.g. BTC/USD.",
      "default": ""
    },
    "qty": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Coin quantity, fractional allowed (0.0015). Leave out and pass --notional to size by dollars."
    },
    "notional": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Size by dollar amount instead of coin quantity."
    },
    "limit": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Limit price. Without it the order is a market order."
    },
    "trigger": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Stop trigger price: with --limit it makes a stop-limit order."
    },
    "stop": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Protective stop price for a buy; the Risk Guardian refuses entries without one."
    },
    "target": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Take-profit price (for the reward:risk check)."
    },
    "tif": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Time in force: gtc (default) or ioc.",
      "default": "gtc"
    },
    "mode": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "sandbox",
        "paper",
        "live"
      ],
      "description": "paper (default) or live (needs a confirmation code). Sandbox does not simulate crypto.",
      "default": "paper"
    },
    "note": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Why: kept in the audit trail."
    },
    "confirmation_code": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Only after the user explicitly approves the preview: the code a previous call of this tool returned."
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "pair"
  ]
}
```

## `diary_export`

Examples:

  idiotproof diary export --csv - --mode live --since 2026-01-01

Changes saved state. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Export your trade diary to a CSV file (ET times, P\u0026L, risk plan, R), or print it with --csv -.",
  "properties": {

      "type": "string",
      "description": "Absolute path of the CSV file to write on the Hub\u0027s machine, or - to return the CSV text.",

      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Replace the file if it already exists.",
      "default": false
    },
    "since": {
      "type": "string",
      "format": "date",
      "description": "First ET date of entry, yyyy-MM-dd (default: everything)."
    },
    "until": {
      "type": "string",
      "format": "date",
      "description": "Last ET date of entry, yyyy-MM-dd (default: today)."
    },
    "mode": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "sandbox",
        "paper",
        "live"
      ],
      "description": "Only trades in this mode: sandbox, paper or live."
    },
    "symbol": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Only this symbol."
    },
    "strategy": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Only this strategy: an id prefix or part of its title at trade time."
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "csv"
  ]
}
```

## `docs_explain`

Explain a type or member: its doc comment, where it is declared (path:line), its members and its callers.

Callers are found by text (every line naming it as a whole word, comments and the declaration skipped), so overloads and same-named members elsewhere also show.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof docs explain <symbol> [--callers <int>]
Examples:
  idiotproof docs explain TransactionGateway
  idiotproof docs explain TransactionGateway.SubmitAsync --callers 5
  idiotproof docs explain T:IdiotProof.Core.Trading.OrderIntent --json

Read-only. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Explain a type or member: its doc comment, where it is declared (path:line), its members and its callers.",
  "properties": {
    "symbol": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "A type or member: TransactionGateway, TransactionGateway.SubmitAsync, a full name, or an XML doc id (T:..., M:...).",
      "default": ""
    },
    "callers": {
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Most lines that mention it to list (default 15; 0 for none).",
      "default": 15
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "symbol"
  ]
}
```

## `docs_search`

Search everything IdiotProof knows about itself: BIBLE, docs, stories, tickets, code docs and catalogs.

Results are ranked: an exact id first, then entries holding every word (title and id hits weigh most). Follow up with `docs law`, `docs section`, `docs story`, `docs ticket` or `docs explain`.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof docs search <text>... [--kind <section|law|doc|story|ticket|symbol|catalog>] [--limit <int>] [--refresh]
Examples:
  idiotproof docs search transaction gateway
  idiotproof docs search "peak giveback" --kind story
  idiotproof docs search IP-LAW-9 --json

Read-only. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Search everything IdiotProof knows about itself: BIBLE, docs, stories, tickets, code docs and catalogs.",
  "properties": {
    "text": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "description": "What to look for: words, a phrase, or an id like IP-LAW-3, IP-US-K1, IP-T259, \u00A74, TransactionGateway."
    },
    "kind": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "section",
        "law",
        "doc",
        "story",
        "ticket",
        "symbol",
        "catalog"
      ],
```

## `gapper_arm`

Arm a gapper: activate an existing one or queue a new one from a profile, honoring one-per-symbol and the 3-gapper cap.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof gapper arm <gapper> [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--profile <string>] [--gap <number>] [--max-gap <number>] [--volume <number>] [--min-price <number>] [--max-price <number>] [--entry-start <string>] [--entry-end <string>] [--stop <number>] [--trail <number>] [--giveback <number>] [--arm-exit <string>] [--sell-by <string>] [--notional <decimal>]
Examples:
  idiotproof gapper arm NVDA
  idiotproof gapper arm ABCD --profile penny-runner --stop 6
  idiotproof gapper arm 0190a3f2

MOVES MONEY. Sandbox and Paper run immediately. A Live action returns status confirmation-required with a preview and a code instead of executing: show the user the preview verbatim, ask them, and only if they say yes call this tool again with the identical arguments plus confirmation_code. Never invent or reuse a code. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Arm a gapper: activate an existing one or queue a new one from a profile, honoring one-per-symbol and the 3-gapper cap.",
  "properties": {
    "gapper": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "A symbol (queues a new gapper when it has none) or a gapper\u0027s id, id prefix or stamp id.",
      "default": ""
    },
    "mode": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "sandbox",
        "paper",
        "live"
      ],
      "description": "Broker mode for a newly queued gapper: paper (default) or sandbox. Live is \u0060strategy mode\u0060, confirmed.",
      "default": "paper"
    },
    "profile": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Gapper profile id or name to start from (default classic-gapper)."
    },
    "gap": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Minimum gap over the previous close, percent."
    },
    "max_gap": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Gap ceiling in percent (0 = no ceiling)."
    },
    "volume": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Premarket volume must be at least this multiple of average volume."
    },
    "min_price": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Lowest price that qualifies."
    },
    "max_price": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Highest price that qualifies."
    },
    "entry_start": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Entry window start, ET (HH:mm)."
    },
    "entry_end": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Entry window end, ET (HH:mm)."
    },
    "stop": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Hard stop below entry, percent."
    },
    "trail": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Trailing stop off the high, percent (0 = none)."
    },
    "giveback": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Sell once price gives back this percent of the entry-to-peak run."
    },
    "arm_exit": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "ET time the giveback exit arms (HH:mm)."
    },
    "sell_by": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Hard flatten time, ET (HH:mm), before the 9:30 bell."
    },
    "notional": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Position size in dollars."
    },
    "confirmation_code": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Only after the user explicitly approves the preview: the code a previous call of this tool returned."
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "gapper"
  ]
}
```

```json
    },
```

```json
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Gapper profile id or name to start from (default classic-gapper)."

      "type": "number",

      "type": "number",
      "description": "Gap ceiling in percent (0 = no ceiling)."

      "type": "number",
      "description": "Premarket volume must be at least this multiple of average volume."
    },
    "min_price": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Lowest price that qualifies."
    },
    "max_price": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Highest price that qualifies."
    },
    "entry_start": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Entry window start, ET (HH:mm)."
    },
    "entry_end": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Entry window end, ET (HH:mm)."
    },
    "stop": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Hard stop below entry, percent."
    },
    "trail": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Trailing stop off the high, percent (0 = none)."
    },
    "giveback": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Sell once price gives back this percent of the entry-to-peak run."
    },
    "arm_exit": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "ET time the giveback exit arms (HH:mm)."
    },
    "sell_by": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Hard flatten time, ET (HH:mm), before the 9:30 bell."
    },
    "notional": {

      "description": "Position size in dollars."
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [

  ]
}
```

## `hub_install_service`

Install the Hub as a Windows service that runs as you (Monitor off unless --monitor).

Runs sc.exe create/description/failure and sets the service's environment in the registry. Needs an elevated Hub; otherwise it prints the commands and points at tools\install-hub-service.ps1, which elevates itself. Grant the account 'Log on as a service' (the script does). Stop any interactive Hub first: both use port 5910.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof hub install-service [--exe <string>] [--account <string>] [--password <string>] [--monitor] [--start <string>] [--dry-run]
Examples:
  idiotproof hub install-service --dry-run
  idiotproof hub install-service --password "..." --monitor

DESTRUCTIVE. If it returns confirmation-required, show the preview and call again with confirmation_code only after the user agrees. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Install the Hub as a Windows service that runs as you (Monitor off unless --monitor).",
  "properties": {
    "exe": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The Hub exe the service runs (default: the published C:\\Apps\\IdiotProof\\Hub\\idiotproof-hub.exe)."
    },
    "account": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Windows account to run as (default: you, as DOMAIN\\user or .\\user). Must be the user who owns the LocalDB database and keys."
    },
    "password": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "That account\u0027s Windows password (required unless --dry-run; never logged)."
    },
    "monitor": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Host the trading Monitor in the service (it places real orders unattended). Off by default.",
      "default": false
    },
    "start": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Start type: delayed-auto (default), auto or demand.",
      "default": "delayed-auto"
    },
    "dry_run": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Show the commands without running them.",
      "default": false
    },
    "confirmation_code": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Only after the user explicitly approves the preview: the code a previous call of this tool returned."
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

## `hub_uninstall_service`

Examples:

```json
    "dry_run": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Show the commands without running them.",
      "default": false
    },
    "confirmation_code": {
      "type": "string",

}
```

## `keys_migrate_to_vault`

Move Alpaca keys, OAuth tokens and Claude keys out of SQL into MindAttic.Vault (dry run unless --apply).

Per user and secret: copy into Vault when Vault lacks it, verify equality when both have it, then clear the SQL column. Conflicts and undecryptable values are reported and left untouched. Idempotent.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof keys migrate-to-vault [--apply]
Examples:
  idiotproof keys migrate-to-vault
  idiotproof keys migrate-to-vault --apply

DESTRUCTIVE. If it returns confirmation-required, show the preview and call again with confirmation_code only after the user agrees. Times are US Eastern.

```json
  "properties": {
    "apply": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Actually copy into Vault and clear the SQL columns (without it: a dry run that changes nothing).",

    },
    "confirmation_code": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Only after the user explicitly approves the preview: the code a previous call of this tool returned."

  },

}
```

```json
    },
```

## `monitor_pause`

Pause the Monitor: from its next tick it evaluates nothing - no entries and NO exits - until resumed.

Sets the SettingsKv flag monitor.paused, honored at the top of every tick (within 2 s). The loop, heartbeat and leader lease stay up. Open positions are not managed while paused - flatten them first if that matters.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof monitor pause [--reason <string>]
Examples:
  idiotproof monitor pause
  idiotproof monitor pause --reason "news pending"

Changes saved state. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Pause the Monitor: from its next tick it evaluates nothing - no entries and NO exits - until resumed.",
  "properties": {
    "reason": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Why (kept with the flag and shown by \u0060monitor status\u0060)."
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

## `monitor_resume`

Resume a paused Monitor (needs a confirmation code when a Live strategy is active).

Clears the SettingsKv flag monitor.paused; the Monitor evaluates again from its next tick. When any active strategy routes Live the first call returns a code: resuming means real-money entries.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof monitor resume
Examples:
  idiotproof monitor resume
  idiotproof monitor resume --confirm K7Q2M9

MOVES MONEY. Sandbox and Paper run immediately. A Live action returns status confirmation-required with a preview and a code instead of executing: show the user the preview verbatim, ask them, and only if they say yes call this tool again with the identical arguments plus confirmation_code. Never invent or reuse a code. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Resume a paused Monitor (needs a confirmation code when a Live strategy is active).",
  "properties": {
    "confirmation_code": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Only after the user explicitly approves the preview: the code a previous call of this tool returned."
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

## `monitor_tick_once`

Run one evaluation pass over your active strategies and show each verdict - never places, cancels or records an order.

Gate 1 only (entry conditions against fresh bars from the Hub's feed); the LLM panel, RiskGuardian and the broker are never called, and no position, progress row or live bar is written. Without --dry the pass is noted in the audit log.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof monitor tick-once [--dry] [--symbol <string>]
Examples:
  idiotproof monitor tick-once --dry
  idiotproof monitor tick-once --symbol NVDA

Read-only. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
```

## `options_buy`

Buy option contracts to open (level 2+). Sandbox by default; live needs a confirmation code.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof options buy <occ> <contracts> [--limit <decimal>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--note <string>]
Examples:
  idiotproof options buy AAPL261219C00150000 2 --limit 3.20 --mode paper
  idiotproof options buy SPY261120P00560000 1 --mode live

MOVES MONEY. Sandbox and Paper run immediately. A Live action returns status confirmation-required with a preview and a code instead of executing: show the user the preview verbatim, ask them, and only if they say yes call this tool again with the identical arguments plus confirmation_code. Never invent or reuse a code. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Buy option contracts to open (level 2\u002B). Sandbox by default; live needs a confirmation code.",
  "properties": {
    "occ": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "OCC contract symbol, e.g. AAPL261219C00150000.",
      "default": ""
    },
    "contracts": {
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Whole contracts (each is usually 100 shares).",
      "default": 0
    },
    "limit": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Limit price per share (premium). Without it the order is a market order."
    },
    "mode": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "sandbox",
        "paper",
        "live"
      ],
      "description": "Where it routes: sandbox (simulator, the default), paper, or live (needs confirmation).",
      "default": "sandbox"
    },
    "note": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Why \u2014 kept in the audit trail."
    },
    "confirmation_code": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Only after the user explicitly approves the preview: the code a previous call of this tool returned."
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "occ",
    "contracts"
  ]
}
```

## `orders_replace`

Change a working order's quantity, limit/stop/trail, TIF or client id (Alpaca PATCH; it gets a new id). Through the gateway; live needs a code.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof orders replace <id> [--qty <decimal>] [--limit <decimal>] [--stop-price <decimal>] [--trail <decimal>] [--tif <string>] [--client-id <string>] [--stop <decimal>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--note <string>]
Examples:
  idiotproof orders replace 61e69015-8549-4bfd-b9c3-01e75843f47d --limit 131.50
  idiotproof orders replace 61e69015-8549-4bfd-b9c3-01e75843f47d --qty 5 --tif gtc --mode live

MOVES MONEY. Sandbox and Paper run immediately. A Live action returns status confirmation-required with a preview and a code instead of executing: show the user the preview verbatim, ask them, and only if they say yes call this tool again with the identical arguments plus confirmation_code. Never invent or reuse a code. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",

  "properties": {
    "id": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The working order to change (from \u0060orders list\u0060).",
      "default": ""
    },
    "qty": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "New share count (fractions allowed)."
    },
    "limit": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "New limit price."
    },
    "stop_price": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "New stop trigger price."
    },
    "trail": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "New trailing distance, in the order\u0027s own unit (percent or dollars)."
    },
    "tif": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "New time in force: day, gtc, opg, cls, ioc or fok."
    },
    "client_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "New client order id for the replacement order."
    },
    "stop": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Protective stop for the position, needed when --qty raises an entry\u0027s size (the Risk Guardian checks the whole new size)."
    },
    "mode": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "sandbox",
        "paper",
        "live"
      ],
      "description": "The account the order is in: paper (default) or live (needs confirmation).",
      "default": "paper"
    },
    "note": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Why \u2014 kept in the audit trail."
    },
    "confirmation_code": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Only after the user explicitly approves the preview: the code a previous call of this tool returned."
    }
  },

}
```

## `strategy_activate`

Hand a strategy to the Monitor. A Live strategy needs a confirmation code.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof strategy activate <strategy>
Examples:
  idiotproof strategy activate NVDA

MOVES MONEY. Sandbox and Paper run immediately. A Live action returns status confirmation-required with a preview and a code instead of executing: show the user the preview verbatim, ask them, and only if they say yes call this tool again with the identical arguments plus confirmation_code. Never invent or reuse a code. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Hand a strategy to the Monitor. A Live strategy needs a confirmation code.",
  "properties": {
    "strategy": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Id, id prefix, stamp id (IP-XXXX-XXXX) or symbol.",
      "default": ""
    },
    "confirmation_code": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Only after the user explicitly approves the preview: the code a previous call of this tool returned."
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "strategy"
  ]
}
```

## `strategy_bulk`

Activate or deactivate many strategies at once (--all, --symbol, --mode). Live activations need one confirmation code for the batch.

Deactivation skips strategies holding a position (that would orphan the exit). Activation skips quarantined and soft-deleted strategies; when the batch would turn on any Live strategy, nothing happens until you re-run with the confirmation code, which is bound to exactly that batch.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof strategy bulk <action> [--all] [--symbol <string>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>]
Examples:
  idiotproof strategy bulk deactivate --all
  idiotproof strategy bulk activate --symbol NVDA --mode paper

MOVES MONEY. Sandbox and Paper run immediately. A Live action returns status confirmation-required with a preview and a code instead of executing: show the user the preview verbatim, ask them, and only if they say yes call this tool again with the identical arguments plus confirmation_code. Never invent or reuse a code. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Activate or deactivate many strategies at once (--all, --symbol, --mode). Live activations need one confirmation code for the batch.",
  "properties": {
    "action": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "activate",
        "deactivate"
      ],
      "description": "activate or deactivate.",
      "default": "activate"
    },
    "all": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Every strategy you own (soft-deleted ones excluded).",
      "default": false
    },
    "symbol": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Only strategies on this symbol."
    },
    "mode": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "sandbox",
        "paper",
        "live"
      ],
      "description": "Only strategies in this broker mode (sandbox, paper, live)."
    },
    "confirmation_code": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Only after the user explicitly approves the preview: the code a previous call of this tool returned."
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "action"
  ]
}
```

## `strategy_clone`

Copy a strategy (optionally onto another symbol) as a new, inactive Sandbox strategy.

The copy gets the same canon (re-validated), never the original's position, history or Live routing. Cloning onto another symbol warns about fixed prices that belonged to the original's chart.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof strategy clone <strategy> [--symbol <string>] [--title <string>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>]
Examples:
  idiotproof strategy clone NVDA
  idiotproof strategy clone NVDA --symbol AMD --title "AMD VWAP reclaim"

Changes saved state. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Copy a strategy (optionally onto another symbol) as a new, inactive Sandbox strategy.",
  "properties": {
    "strategy": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Id, id prefix, stamp id or symbol of the strategy to copy.",
      "default": ""
    },
    "symbol": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Trade a different symbol with the same rules."
    },
    "title": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Title for the copy (default: \u0022\u003Ctitle\u003E (copy)\u0022)."
    },
    "mode": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "sandbox",
        "paper",
        "live"
      ],
      "description": "Broker mode for the copy: sandbox (default) or paper.",
      "default": "sandbox"
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "strategy"
  ]
}
```

## `strategy_create`

Create a strategy from IdiotScript or canonical JSON after validating it. It starts inactive in Sandbox.

Exactly one of --script or --canon. A strategy with no size buys 1 share. Errors (no stop, stop on the wrong side of the target, a broken canon) stop the save; warnings are shown.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof strategy create [--script <string>] [--canon <string>] [--title <string>] [--ticker <string>] [--description <string>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--dry-run]
Examples:
  idiotproof strategy create --script "Stock.Ticker(\"NVDA\").IsAboveVwap().Long().StopLoss(170).TakeProfit(190).Build()"
  idiotproof strategy create --canon - --mode paper

Changes saved state. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Create a strategy from IdiotScript or canonical JSON after validating it. It starts inactive in Sandbox.",
  "properties": {
    "script": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The strategy as IdiotScript text (\u0060-\u0060 reads stdin)."
    },
    "canon": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The strategy as canonical JSON (what \u0060strategy export --format json\u0060 prints) (\u0060-\u0060 reads stdin)."
    },
    "title": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Title (default: the strategy\u0027s own name, else \u0022SYM strategy\u0022)."
    },
    "ticker": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Symbol to use when the script doesn\u0027t name one."
    },
    "description": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Free-form description stored with the strategy."
    },
    "mode": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "sandbox",
        "paper",
        "live"
      ],
      "description": "Broker mode: sandbox (default) or paper. Live is a separate, confirmed step.",
      "default": "sandbox"
    },
    "dry_run": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Validate and show the stamp without saving anything.",
      "default": false
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

## `strategy_delete`

Soft-delete a strategy: deactivate it and mark it [deleted] (reversible with --restore). Refused while it holds a position.

Deleting is a reversible disable (HOUSE-LAW-2): the row, canon and history stay, and `strategy list` hides it unless --deleted. --hard permanently removes a strategy that is already deleted — a separate, explicit second step.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof strategy delete <strategy> [--restore] [--hard]
Examples:
  idiotproof strategy delete NVDA
  idiotproof strategy delete 0193ab12 --restore
  idiotproof strategy delete 0193ab12 --hard

DESTRUCTIVE. If it returns confirmation-required, show the preview and call again with confirmation_code only after the user agrees. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Soft-delete a strategy: deactivate it and mark it [deleted] (reversible with --restore). Refused while it holds a position.",
  "properties": {
    "strategy": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Id, id prefix, stamp id or symbol.",
      "default": ""
    },
    "restore": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Undo a delete: take the [deleted] marker off (it stays inactive).",
      "default": false
    },
    "hard": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Permanently remove an ALREADY deleted strategy and its progress row. Cannot be undone.",
      "default": false
    },
    "confirmation_code": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Only after the user explicitly approves the preview: the code a previous call of this tool returned."
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "strategy"
  ]
}
```

## `strategy_from_text`

Turn a plain-English description into a strategy (via the LLM), show its stamp, and save it only when you confirm.

The first call writes the IdiotScript, validates it and shows the stamp with a confirmation code; nothing is saved. Re-run with --confirm <code> to save exactly what was shown (the LLM is not called again). It saves inactive, in Sandbox by default, 1 share when unsized.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof strategy from-text <description> [--ticker <string>] [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--title <string>]
Examples:
  idiotproof strategy from-text "Buy NVDA when it reclaims VWAP with volume, stop 2% under, take profit at 190"
  idiotproof strategy from-text "long on a 9 EMA reclaim above VWAP, 3% stop" --ticker AMD --mode paper

Changes saved state. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Turn a plain-English description into a strategy (via the LLM), show its stamp, and save it only when you confirm.",
  "properties": {
    "description": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The strategy in plain English (\u0060-\u0060 reads stdin).",
      "default": ""
    },
    "ticker": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The symbol to trade (default: the first ticker-looking word, e.g. $NVDA or NVDA)."
    },
    "mode": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "sandbox",
        "paper",
        "live"
      ],
      "description": "Broker mode for the saved strategy: sandbox (default) or paper.",
      "default": "sandbox"
    },
    "title": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Title for the saved strategy (default: its own name, else \u0022SYM strategy\u0022)."
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "description"
  ]
}
```

## `strategy_from_watchlist`

Create one strategy per item of a watchlist JSON file (the Monitor's create-strategies, through the CLI).

Each item's script is validated like `strategy create`; an item that fails is reported and skipped. Items already present (same symbol and title) or repeated in the file are skipped, so re-running is safe. New strategies start inactive in Sandbox with 1 share when unsized; --activate turns on the items marked active.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof strategy from-watchlist <file> [--mode <sandbox|paper|live>] [--activate] [--dry-run]
Examples:
  idiotproof strategy from-watchlist D:/watchlists/2026-10-30.json
  idiotproof strategy from-watchlist -
  idiotproof strategy from-watchlist - --mode paper --activate --dry-run

Changes saved state. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Create one strategy per item of a watchlist JSON file (the Monitor\u0027s create-strategies, through the CLI).",
  "properties": {
    "file": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "A watchlist JSON file (absolute path: the Hub reads it), the JSON itself, or \u0060-\u0060 for stdin: [{\u0022title\u0022,\u0022symbol\u0022,\u0022script\u0022,\u0022description\u0022,\u0022author\u0022,\u0022originTranscript\u0022,\u0022active\u0022}].",
      "default": ""
    },
    "mode": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "sandbox",
        "paper",
        "live"
      ],
      "description": "Broker mode for every new strategy: sandbox (default) or paper.",
      "default": "sandbox"
    },
    "activate": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Activate items marked \u0022active\u0022: true (default: everything starts inactive).",
      "default": false
    },
    "dry_run": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Validate every item and report what would happen without saving.",
      "default": false
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "file"
  ]
}
```

## `strategy_progress`

Reads the row the Monitor writes every tick. --watch samples it --samples times, --every seconds apart (at most two minutes in all), and reports each change; it stops early when every condition passes.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof strategy progress <strategy> [--watch] [--every <int>] [--samples <int>]
Examples:

  idiotproof strategy progress NVDA --watch --every 10 --samples 6

## `strategy_resync_canon`

Re-derive your strategies' canons from their scripts where the script now yields a richer canon; dry run unless --apply.

The repair for verbs an older parser dropped silently. A row is rewritten only when the re-derived canon has at least as many entry conditions and branches as the stored one; anything that would lose a condition is skipped and reported. Only the canon (ScriptJson) changes — position bookkeeping is untouched.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof strategy resync-canon [--apply]
Examples:
  idiotproof strategy resync-canon
  idiotproof strategy resync-canon --apply

Changes saved state. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Re-derive your strategies\u0027 canons from their scripts where the script now yields a richer canon; dry run unless --apply.",
  "properties": {
    "apply": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Write the repaired canons (default is a dry run that changes nothing).",
      "default": false
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

## `strategy_set`

Edit a strategy's stop, target, trailing, size, sell-by time or session; the canon is rewritten and re-validated.

Only the named fields change. The result must still validate (a stop, stop below target on a long, ...). A Live strategy needs a confirmation code bound to exactly these changes.

CLI equivalent: idiotproof strategy set <strategy> [--stop <decimal>] [--stop-percent <decimal>] [--target <decimal>] [--target-percent <decimal>] [--trailing <decimal>] [--giveback <decimal>] [--qty <int>] [--notional <decimal>] [--sell-by <string>] [--session <premarket|rth|after-hours|extended>]
Examples:
  idiotproof strategy set NVDA --stop 168.5 --target 195
  idiotproof strategy set NVDA --qty 2 --sell-by 15:45

MOVES MONEY. Sandbox and Paper run immediately. A Live action returns status confirmation-required with a preview and a code instead of executing: show the user the preview verbatim, ask them, and only if they say yes call this tool again with the identical arguments plus confirmation_code. Never invent or reuse a code. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Edit a strategy\u0027s stop, target, trailing, size, sell-by time or session; the canon is rewritten and re-validated.",
  "properties": {
    "strategy": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Id, id prefix, stamp id or symbol.",
      "default": ""
    },
    "stop": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Stop-loss price (replaces a percent stop)."
    },
    "stop_percent": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Stop-loss percent from the fill (replaces a price stop)."
    },
    "target": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Take-profit price (replaces a percent target and any scale-out ladder)."
    },
    "target_percent": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Take-profit percent from the fill (replaces a price target)."
    },
    "trailing": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Trailing-stop percent; 0 removes it."
    },
    "giveback": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Peak-giveback exit percent; 0 removes it."
    },
    "qty": {
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Share quantity per entry (replaces a notional size)."
    },
    "notional": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Dollar size per entry (replaces a share quantity)."
    },
    "sell_by": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Sell anything still held at this ET time (HH:mm); \u0022none\u0022 removes it."
    },
    "session": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "premarket",
        "rth",
        "after-hours",
        "extended"
      ],
      "description": "Trading session: premarket, rth, afterhours or extended."
    },
    "confirmation_code": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Only after the user explicitly approves the preview: the code a previous call of this tool returned."
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "strategy"
  ]
}
```

```json
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Create an IdiotProof account (blocklist and password rules of web sign-up; Argon2id via MindAttic.Authentication).",
  "properties": {
    "email": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The new account\u0027s email (also its user name).",
      "default": ""
    },
    "password": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Initial password: 8 to 128 characters with at least one digit.",
      "default": ""
    },
    "role": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "User (default) or Admin.",
      "default": "User"
    },
    "must_change": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Make them choose a new password at first sign-in.",
      "default": false
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "email",
    "password"
  ]
}
```

## `users_list`

List the IdiotProof accounts (test fixtures hidden unless --all); * marks who you act as.

  idiotproof users list --all

Read-only. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "List the IdiotProof accounts (test fixtures hidden unless --all); * marks who you act as.",
  "properties": {
    "all": {
      "type": "boolean",

    }

  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

## `watchlist_add`

Add symbols to your IdiotProof watchlist (creates a 'Main' workspace when you have none).

CLI equivalent: idiotproof watchlist add <symbols>... [--workspace <string>]
Examples:
  idiotproof watchlist add NVDA AAPL
  idiotproof watchlist add TSLA --workspace Main

Changes saved state. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Add symbols to your IdiotProof watchlist (creates a \u0027Main\u0027 workspace when you have none).",
  "properties": {
    "symbols": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "description": "One or more ticker symbols (space or comma separated)."
    },
    "workspace": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Which workspace (name or id); needed only when you have more than one."
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "symbols"
  ]
}
```

## `watchlists_delete`

Delete an Alpaca watchlist (by id or name).

CLI equivalent: idiotproof watchlists delete <watchlist> [--mode <paper|live>]
Examples:
  idiotproof watchlists delete tech

DESTRUCTIVE. If it returns confirmation-required, show the preview and call again with confirmation_code only after the user agrees. Times are US Eastern.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Delete an Alpaca watchlist (by id or name).",
  "properties": {
    "watchlist": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Watchlist id or name.",
      "default": ""
    },
    "mode": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "paper",
        "live"
      ],
      "description": "Alpaca account: paper (default) or live.",
      "default": "paper"
    },
    "confirmation_code": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Only after the user explicitly approves the preview: the code a previous call of this tool returned."
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "watchlist"
  ]
}
```
